Posted April 11, 2003
Special report to MarijuanaNews.com by Richard Cowan

The Kubby refugee hearings today should have been pointless, but ended up making a very important point.
See
 DEAland On Trial At Kubby Refugee Hearings. Damning Testimony From A Patient, A Judge and Ed Rosenthal. Meanwhile, Congress Was Busy Making It Even Worse. Special Report to MarijuanaNews.com

The first witness called by Immigration was the Canadian cancer specialist, Dr. Joseph Connors of the B.C. Cancer Agency, who is now Steve's doctor here in Canada. Michele Kubby declined to ask him any questions, because his written diagnosis is a part of the record, and she argued that one reason doctors are so reluctant to take medical cannabis patients is the fear of being called to some hearing. Even if doctors are not intimidated, most are so busy that they are understandably reluctant to take half a day away from their practice to answer unnecessary questions. (He was present in the hearing room.)

Of course, he confirmed his diagnosis and approval of Steve's use of cannabis, because it has been controlling his symptoms for many years after almost all adrenal cancer victims have died. It was quite clear that he and other doctors who have seen Steve here have been very thorough in their examinations. In short, there is absolutely no doubt about either Steve's condition or that it responds to cannabis.

The other witness, who testified by phone, was Chris Cattran, the Assistant DA from Placer County who prosecuted the Kubbys.
See
 Local Editor Says Kubby Prosecution Ends with a Whimper.

He really had little to add to the record. However, one point that Michele raised offered an insight into how arbitrary Placer's medical cannabis policies remain to this day.

The county has no written guidelines on the amount of cannabis a patient may have, so patients can never know if they are in compliance.

Instead, the limit is supposedly that which a patient might reasonably be expected to need for his condition.

Well, that sounds reasonable by definition.

But who decides what the patient needs? A nark, of course.

(The same nark is also supposedly an authority on plant yields and said that each plant would yield 3 to 6 ounces per plant. Prop 215 has no limit on the number of plants a patient can have, and absent proof of selling, there is really no justification for any interference in a patients growing under the law. Not that the law carries much weight in Placer county.)

In the real world, even a doctor who is very knowledgeable about medical cannabis could not make such a judgment without consulting the patient. Some patients need just a little, while others need much more, even for the same conditions.

It is virtually certain that the nark who was the expert who decided how much Steve needed, would never have heard of his very rare condition. Even the leading BC cancer specialist, who sees virtually everyone in the province with his type of cancer, said that he finds only two or three such cases per year.

How can the patients challenge the nark's opinion on how much cannabis they need? In criminal court, of course! What a wonderful diagnostic procedure. Needless to say, the prosecution will also try to offer its own diagnosis, and turns out that they made just such an effort in the Kubby case.

Cattran explained that they had arranged for two specialists to fly in and testify about Steve's condition and his use of cannabis, but, at the last minute, the judge decided at the last minute not to allow the challenge to Steve's doctors. Perhaps one reason that the judge decided not to allow this challenge was because the doctors had never examined Steve.
See
Prominent Cancer Specialist Says Steve Kubby Should Be Studied, Not Jailed;
His Case Has Major Medical Implications.

The Immigration attorney should have left it at that, but

Instead, he asked Cattran if he knew what these two psychic doctors were going to say.

Yes, he replied. They were going to say that Steve didn't have cancer, but if he did, cannabis was contraindicated and would just make his condition worse! The fact that the leading cancer specialist in BC had just testified to the contrary was not lost on the Adjudicator.

The fact that much of California law enforcement is still not obeying the law, and is still placing the lives of patients in danger should not be lost on anyone.

(MarijuanaNews note: The hearings will continue next week, but I will be in San Francisco for the NORML conference. I hope to see you there. I will be doing reports every day, I hope.)

Also please see
